question: In the package that exposes etcd's monitoring endpoints over plain HTTP there is one exported wiring routine. Given a logger, a request multiplexer and a narrow server interface (alarms, current leader, a range call, the server config, the auth store and learner status), it registers the aggregate status endpoint -- backed by an inline closure that screens alarms first, then leadership, then issues a real v3 range request with its own timeout -- and then installs the two per-check endpoint trees for liveness and readiness. It returns nothing; its whole purpose is the registration side effect on the multiplexer. Name every function or method in the corpus that calls it, each as path::name. Count every call in the corpus, including callers in test files and in the file that defines it, and name each caller once.

question: In the write-ahead log package there is an unexported constructor over an already-open file handle. It asks the operating system where that handle currently sits, and on success hands back a record-writing object whose page-aligned buffered writer is primed at exactly that byte offset and whose running checksum chains from a caller-supplied seed; if the position query fails it yields no object and the underlying error instead. It exists so that appending can resume in the middle of an existing segment on a correct page boundary rather than from byte zero, and it is a thin wrapper over the plain in-memory variant that takes an explicit offset argument. Name every function or method in the corpus that calls it, each as path::name. Count every call in the corpus, including callers in test files and in the file that defines it, and name each caller once.

question: Inside the package that owns the backend's bucket layout and its upgrade/downgrade machinery sits an exported lock-free accessor. question: In the package that models etcd's server, cluster and storage version state machine there is an exported two-argument predicate over semantic versions. Everything else is false -- equal operands, patch-only movement, and any jump across major numbers. It guards the moment a member swaps in a new capability table and the moment the background monitor settles on a newly agreed value for the whole membership. question: The multi-version store writes every revision as a fixed-width big-endian byte key, and a slightly longer variant of that key appends a separator plus a one-byte marker meaning the entry records a deletion rather than a live value. It is consulted when a raw key is decoded into its structured form, twice while the backend is replayed into the in-memory key index, once while a scanned batch of backend rows is fanned out for that replay, and once when raw revision/value pairs are turned into events for watchers. question: One exported function in the write-ahead log package tries to rescue a log directory whose final segment was cut short by a crash mid-write. It tolerates a nil logger, opens the last segment for read-write, and streams records through a decoder, keeping the running checksum in step and validating any checksum record it meets. A clean end of stream means the directory was already sound and it reports success; an unexpected end of stream mid-record means the tail is torn, so it copies the entire segment aside under a '.broken' suffix with private permissions, rewinds, trims the original at the last good record offset, syncs it, and reports whether that rescue went through. Anything else -- the directory vanishing, a checksum mismatch, a failed copy -- reports failure. Its whole result is a single boolean. Name every function or method in the corpus that calls it, each as path::name. Count every call in the corpus, including callers in test files and in the file that defines it, and name each caller once.

question: In the v3 gRPC API layer of the server there is a small unexported two-argument predicate, living in the package's grab-bag utility file next to the error-translation table. question: In the server-side versioning package, a small type wraps an abstraction over the cluster and on-disk state and reconciles the two. When nothing is recorded yet, or the pair differs, it logs the discrepancy, asks the wrapped abstraction to write the cluster's major and minor with a zero patch, returns early after logging if that write fails, and finally, when a downgrade is in progress, logs that this server is now ready to move down. question: In the automatic compaction package, the periodic strategy keeps a sliding window of sampled revisions. One unexported no-argument accessor on that strategy computes the sampling step it waits between samples: it takes the configured retention period, clamps it to at most one hour if it is larger, then divides the clamped value by a package-level constant divisor of ten, and yields the resulting `time.Duration`. It sits directly beside a near-identical twin that applies the same clamp but hands back the whole undivided interval; this one is the one-tenth value, also reused as the retry delay after a failed compaction and as the denominator when sizing the sample window. Test code advances a fake clock by exactly this amount to simulate elapsed time. Name every function or method in the corpus that calls it, each as path::name. Count every call in the corpus, including callers in test files and in the file that defines it, and name each caller once.
author_notes: The production call at periodic.go:102 is in `Run`, whose body is almost entirely a `go func() { ... }()` goroutine spanning lines 105-161; the call itself is above the goroutine but the surrounding text is dominated by it, and the nearest `func` token below is the closure. question: In the write-ahead log package, the record reader carries a rolling checksum accumulator over the records it consumes.
